name: filter, map, collect
desc: Keeps the rows that pass, changes what each row is, and stores the result. Nothing runs until the terminal operation.
body: Order matters. `filter` before `map` keeps the lambdas small and drops rows before any conversion, while `map` before `filter` forces the test to read the new element type. The source list is never changed, and the whole chain runs once, at the terminal call.

name: flatMap()
desc: Turns each element into a stream and joins those streams into one. Use it when a field holds a collection.
body:
`map(b -> b.guests())` gives a `Stream<List<String>>`. `flatMap` gives a `Stream<String>`, which is what `distinct`, `sorted`, and `joining` need. Inside `groupingBy`, `Collectors.flatMapping` does the same job per group.

A row whose list is empty contributes nothing, so the result never contains a null element produced by an empty collection.

name: groupingBy with a downstream
desc: Groups rows by a key and applies a collector to each group, so one pass can produce counts, sums, or sets instead of lists.
body:
The classifier builds the key, the downstream decides the value. A null key from the classifier throws `NullPointerException` before any collector runs, so filter those rows out or default the field.

Nesting works by passing another `groupingBy` as the downstream:

```java
Map<String, Map<String, Long>> perCity = bookings.stream()
        .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(Booking::city,
                Collectors.groupingBy(Booking::hotel, Collectors.counting())));
```

name: partitioningBy()
desc: Splits the stream into two groups on a boolean. The result always holds both keys, even when one side is empty.
body: Both keys are always present, so `map.get(true)` never returns null. That is the difference from `groupingBy`, which drops a key that never occurs. The downstream forms (`counting`, `averagingInt`, `filtering`, `mapping`) avoid a second pass over the rows.

name: toMap with a merge function
desc: Builds a map from the rows. The merge function decides what happens when two rows produce the same key.
body:
Without the merge function a repeated key throws `IllegalStateException: Duplicate key`. `Integer::sum` and `(left, right) -> left + right` are the same merge here. The merge function is also where a different rule lives, such as keeping the later row with `(left, right) -> right`.

The fourth argument is optional and changes only the map implementation, for example `TreeMap::new` for sorted keys.

name: sum, average, summaryStatistics
desc: Reduces a numeric field to one number. A primitive stream unlocks sum, average, min, max, and all five statistics in one pass.
body:
`sum()` returns `0` for an empty stream while `average()` returns an empty `OptionalDouble`, so the two need different empty handling. `summaryStatistics()` computes count, sum, min, max, and average in one traversal.

The grouped forms take the field directly, for example `Collectors.summingInt(Booking::total)` or `Collectors.averagingInt(Booking::nights)`.

name: max() and min()
desc: Returns the largest or smallest element by a comparator, wrapped in Optional because the stream may be empty.
body:
Both terminals return `Optional<T>`, never a bare element, so the empty case is visible in the return type. `Comparator.comparingInt` reads an int field without boxing it.

For a top list, sort with `Comparator.comparingInt(Booking::nights).reversed()` and then `limit(n)`. `max` returns one element, not a ranking.

name: reduce()
desc: Folds every element into one value. With an identity the result is never Optional; without one it is empty for an empty stream.
body:
With an identity the result type is the identity type, and an empty stream returns that identity. Without one the result is `Optional`, because there is nothing to return.

The three argument form adds a combiner. A parallel stream uses it to join partial results, so the accumulator and the combiner must agree or the sequential and parallel answers differ.

name: sorted, distinct, limit
desc: Orders the stream, removes duplicates by equals, and cuts it short. The position of each step changes the result.
body:
`distinct` uses `equals` and `hashCode`, so it only removes duplicates that the class actually defines. `sorted()` with no argument needs a `Comparable` element type and throws `ClassCastException` otherwise.

`limit` cuts at its own position in the chain. `distinct` before `limit` fills the count with different values, `limit` before `distinct` can return fewer rows than asked for.

name: Optional map, flatMap, orElse
desc: Carries a value that may be missing through a chain of transformations and opens the box exactly once, at the end.
body:
`map` transforms a present value and leaves an empty box alone; `flatMap` is for a function that already returns `Optional`, such as a lookup or `Optional.ofNullable` on a nullable column.

`orElse` builds its argument every time, `orElseGet` only when the value is missing. `Optional.stream()` turns zero or one value into a stream, which lets `flatMap` drop the misses out of a longer pipeline.

name: parallelStream()
desc: Splits the source across the fork join pool. It pays for large CPU bound work with independent elements and breaks on shared mutable state.
body:
`parallelStream()` splits the source across the common fork join pool. It pays for large CPU bound work and costs more than it saves on a small list or on IO.

`collect`, `reduce`, and `count` are safe because each thread owns a partial result. `forEach` writing into a shared `ArrayList` loses rows, since several threads resize the array at the same time. Use `collect(Collectors.toList())` instead.

name: Group, sort entries, join
desc: Builds a text report: group the rows, sort the entries by value, format each line, and join them into one string.
body:
A map cannot be sorted directly, so the second half streams its `entrySet`. `Map.Entry.comparingByValue()` needs the type argument when the compiler cannot infer it, hence `Map.Entry.<String, Integer>comparingByValue().reversed()`.

Sorting by value descending and then joining with `\n` is the shortest path from a grouped map to a printed report. Add `.thenComparing(Map.Entry.comparingByKey())` to break ties in a fixed order.
